# Platform and Organism Identification for GEO Series GSE309890

## Abstract

This report resolves two metadata attributes of a single Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series record, GSE309890: the sequencing platform on which it was run and the organism from which its samples derive. The query was routed to NCBI GEO through two record-retrieval calls, the first on the Series accession and the second on the Platform accession returned by it. GSE309890 is registered under platform GPL24659, which GEO titles "Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655)". The organism recorded in the Series `taxon` field is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, matching the taxon registered on the platform record. The Series comprises 6 samples (GSM9284457–GSM9284462) split between 3 control replicates and 3 replicates of a 40-day adaptive-evolution condition, and is classified as "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing". The study concerns sertraline-biased emergence of antibiotic resistance in *E. coli* and the role of the pentose phosphate pathway enzyme transketolase A. The record has a public date of 2026/02/01, is linked to BioProject PRJNA1363958, and carries no linked PubMed record. The result matters because platform and taxon determine whether a dataset can be integrated with others: GPL24659 hosts 460 samples in total, so GSE309890 is comparable, at the platform level, with a substantial body of existing *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 data.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 is a GEO Series deposited to study how the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor sertraline biases antibiotic resistance emergence in *Escherichia coli*. Per the record summary, sertraline exposure produced early accumulation of rifampicin- and ciprofloxacin-targeting mutations, coupled to a Complex I-dependent respiratory shift and a redirection of glucose from glycolysis into the pentose phosphate pathway; inhibition of transketolase A (tktA) abolished the sertraline-primed survival advantage. Identifying the platform and organism is the prerequisite step for any reuse of the deposited expression values, since platform determines read chemistry and probe/feature space and taxon determines the reference annotation.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. The GEO record explicitly reports no linked PubMed record ("No PubMed record is linked to this GEO record"), which the tool notes typically indicates an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before the query, the platform identifier and the specific *E. coli* strain behind GSE309890 were unknown, and the platform accession alone (GPL24659) does not name an instrument without a second lookup.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: retrieve the `platform` and `taxon` fields of GSE309890 from GEO, and resolve the platform accession to its instrument name. Expectation: the taxon on the Series and the taxon on the Platform record agree, since GEO platform records are strain-scoped.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The question is a metadata lookup on one named GEO accession. It was routed to NCBI GEO directly rather than to a federated dataset index, because GEO is the authoritative source for Series and Platform records and returns both fields in one summary call. A second call was required because the Series record reports the platform only as an accession, not as an instrument name.

**Materials.**
- NCBI GEO (`gds` Entrez database), reached with the `geo_series` tool.

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true [default])` — returned the Series summary, including `taxon`, `platform`, `sample_count`, `samples`, `experiment_type`, `bioproject`, `pubmed_ids`, and the supplementary file listing. Underlying API call: `esummary.fcgi`, `db=gds`, `id=200309890`, `version=2.0`.
2. `geo_series(accession="GPL24659")` — the platform accession returned by step 1, resolved to its Platform record to obtain the instrument name and platform-level taxon and sample count. Underlying API call: `esummary.fcgi`, `db=gds`, `id=100024659`, `version=2.0`.

No filters, date ranges, or search terms were applied; both calls were direct accession retrievals.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. All values are single field reads from two esummary records. The sample count of 6 is the `sample_count` field of the Series record and is corroborated by the 6 distinct GSM accessions enumerated in the `samples` array (no duplicates present). The 3/3 condition split was derived by reading the `title` string of each of those 6 sample entries. The platform-level figure of 460 is the `sample_count` field of the GPL24659 record and covers all Series using that platform, not GSE309890 alone. No percentages were calculated.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Queried fields of GEO Series GSE309890 and its platform record.**

| Field | Series GSE309890 | Platform GPL24659 |
|---|---|---|
| Accession | GSE309890 | GPL24659 |
| Entrez UID | 200309890 | 100024659 |
| Entry type | Series (GSE) | Platform (GPL) |
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback | Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655) |
| Taxon | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Platform | GPL24659 | GPL24659 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | (not populated) |
| Sample count | 6 | 460 |
| Public date | 2026/02/01 | 2018/02/26 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | none | none |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 | (not applicable) |

**Table 2. Samples in GSE309890.**

| GSM accession | Sample title | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| GSM9284457 | E. coli, control,rep1 | Control |
| GSM9284458 | E. coli, control,rep2 | Control |
| GSM9284459 | E. coli, control,rep3 | Control |
| GSM9284460 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 | Adaptive evolution, 40 day |
| GSM9284461 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 | Adaptive evolution, 40 day |
| GSM9284462 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 | Adaptive evolution, 40 day |

**Findings.**

GSE309890 was run on platform GPL24659, titled "Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655)". The instrument is the Illumina HiSeq 4000.

The organism is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. This value appears in the `taxon` field of both the Series record and the Platform record.

The Series holds 6 samples: 3 control replicates and 3 replicates from a 40-day adaptive evolution condition. The experiment type is "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing". The Series public date is 2026/02/01; the Platform public date is 2018/02/26. GPL24659 carries 460 samples across all Series that use it, of which the 6 in GSE309890 are a subset.

The record has no linked PubMed IDs. It is linked to BioProject PRJNA1363958. One supplementary file is present, `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz` (510K, last modified 2025-11-14 11:10), which the tool identifies as the only location of the processed expression values.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Both objectives are met by direct field reads. The platform is Illumina HiSeq 4000 and the organism is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The stated expectation held: the Series taxon and the Platform taxon are identical strings, consistent with GEO platform records being scoped to a single strain for prokaryotic sequencing platforms.

**Context.** The organism assignment is coherent with the Series summary, which describes experiments in *E. coli* involving rifampicin and ciprofloxacin resistance and manipulation of transketolase A. The short-read Illumina platform is consistent with the declared experiment type of expression profiling by high throughput sequencing and with the deposited FPKM matrix.

**Limitations.** The two calls return esummary metadata only. As the tool states, GEO's API returns metadata only, and the processed expression values exist solely in the supplementary file on the FTP tree; nothing here verifies the contents of that file. The absence of linked PubMed IDs is reported by the tool as meaning no link is registered in GEO, which "never means the study has no data" — it does not establish that the study is unpublished. The platform title names the instrument as submitters registered it; per-run instrument details (read length, paired vs single end) are not in the Series esummary and would require the SRA or BioProject records. The 460 figure describes GPL24659 as a whole and says nothing about GSE309890's quality or comparability beyond shared platform. The 3/3 condition split is inferred from free-text sample titles, which are submitter-supplied, not a controlled field.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 is an Illumina HiSeq 4000 (GPL24659) expression study of *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 with 6 samples. The next queries worth running are a retrieval of the runs under BioProject PRJNA1363958 to obtain per-run library layout, instrument model and FASTQ paths, and a GEO search restricted to organism *Escherichia coli* with platform GPL24659 to enumerate the comparable Series available for joint reanalysis.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, Series GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO, Platform GPL24659. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GPL24659
[3] NCBI E-utilities esummary (db=gds, id=200309890, version=2.0). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[4] NCBI E-utilities esummary (db=gds, id=100024659, version=2.0). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[5] NCBI GEO FTP, GSE309890 series directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[6] NCBI GEO FTP, GSE309890 supplementary file GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[7] NCBI GEO FTP, GPL24659 platform directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/platforms/GPL24nnn/GPL24659/

## Acknowledgments

Records used here were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus and served through NCBI E-utilities. The underlying Series was deposited by the submitters of GSE309890 and BioProject PRJNA1363958.
